callbacks.result_semantics: Replace an item handle with force-release success one, or zero when unavailable or unreleasable.
preconditions: The caller has initialized live RuntimeObjectPrefix and ActorScriptState storage with a live saved VM and writable value buffer. The declared operands and result lie above protected locals and frame metadata. Item/owner/action/audio/camera/global data and C-stack storage used by each helper are disjoint from VM contexts, values, protected frames and program storage. Numeric operands use signed 32-bit integer conversion. Integer and code-reference values are signed scalars; finite floats must fit signed 32-bit integers and are truncated. Strings and arbitrary pointer conversions are unsupported.

itemTryRelease with force one rejects ownership states 4 and 5; valid states 0 through 3 proceed. Player ownership (1) clears gPlayerHeldItemHandle at 0x800EF724. Actor ownership (2 or 3) resolves the owner handle and clears the live owner ActorScriptState.heldItemHandle at offset 0x190, including when the owner is the caller. A missing owner does not prevent release. Every live owner has a valid, stable actor-layout held-item field. Owner lookup does not establish runtime kind, so that layout is an explicit prerequisite.

Use the original 166-entry ItemKind.release column at offset 0x48. Only kind 49 selects lightBulbResetReleasedGlow at 0x80123140, and kind 80 selects baseballCapResetReleasedScale at 0x80123060; all other release hooks are null. Arbitrary callback substitution is excluded. These hooks inspect ownership before release resets it: only Pikachu ownership (2) triggers the bulb material-animation reset to 0xF3 or the cap scale reset to one. Hold, launch, collision and update hooks are not invoked by this native.

The cap callback calls itemSetScale, which restores the root radius from state.baseRadius, sets uniform scale to area.objectScale multiplied by the catalog scale, then recursively scales and halves root and child bounds. Area and catalog scales and bounds must be initialized and finite, and the hierarchy must be acyclic. This describes the helper’s writes; it does not promise that every child bound returns to its original value. The bulb callback initializes the material track from borrowed animation program 0xF3 and sets its active halfword to one. That program must be valid, its jumps must terminate, interpolation must be representable, and interpolation duration must be nonzero. Evaluation with step zero is deterministic and performs no RNG update, allocation or callback.

A release callback receives the item and former holder address by value. Both retail hooks ignore the holder argument and retain no C-stack pointer. After the hook, release writes world ownership (0), owner zero, modeTime zero and ground-and-air mode (0), then clears the transfer-permission bit. Mode zero recursively clears hierarchy flags 0x700 only when the root has at least one of those bits; otherwise child-only bits remain unchanged. Release performs no collision registration, unregister operation, search-tree mutation, item-count change or resource free.

No item allocation, deletion, physical attachment-matrix update, hold callback, game-mode change, message, audio operation, OS queue operation or DMA occurs synchronously. Items remain live borrowed objects whose ownership fields have changed; returning does not extend their lifetimes. Future held-item, update and rendering callbacks and their borrowed animation or model resources are outside this immediate footprint and require independent lifetime checks. Original SDK memory-primitive semantics and strict matching authentication remain required. No runtime claim is made.

A resolved candidate must be a genuine initialized runtime item with stable ItemStatePrefix and catalog kind zero through 165. The available resolver rejects zero, missing, destruction-marked and toolbox-owned items, but does not enforce item type. Arbitrary non-item objects are unsupported. The object pool is initialized with positive capacity and valid acyclic chains; lookup writes only local predecessor output.

Force one bypasses transfer-permission gating for eligible ownership states. Suspended ownership (5) still returns zero without releasing; toolbox ownership (4) is already excluded by the resolver. World ownership can return one and invoke its fixed retail release hook even if not currently held. The native reports itemTryRelease success directly rather than returning item kind, and does not perform pickup or replacement.
